🚨🌎 IRAN DECLARES VICTORY — "THE ENEMY'S OBJECTIVES REDUCED TO NOTHING"

After four months of US and Israeli airstrikes that killed Supreme Leader Khamenei on February 28, destroyed military infrastructure, and blockaded the Strait of Hormuz — Iran survived and got a peace deal.

Deputy FM Kazem Gharibabadi: "The enemy, which attacked to carry out its evil designs, has seen all its objectives reduced to nothing, and the Islamic Republic of Iran has achieved great victories in this war."

Signing in Geneva, June 19. Khamenei's funeral set for July 9.

CENTER FOR INTERNATIONAL POLICY: Arming the Cartels – and so many others
June 15, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Rare fair US-side analysis. John Lindsay-Poland names what most US outlets won't: Sig Sauer and Glock exporting to compromised Sinaloa police, Barrett .50 calibers sold without background checks in Arizona and Texas — the cartel armory next door.

🇲🇽 Missing piece: Mexico's lawsuits against US gunmakers (Smith & Wesson) and the SCOTUS dismissal go unmentioned. Sheinbaum has continued pressing the legal angle internationally.

• "Between 70% and 80% of firearms seized in Mexico and submitted for tracing came from the United States"
• "62% of U.S.-sourced guns with a time-to-crime of a year or less were procured from Arizona"

LATIN TIMES: The World Cup Returned to Mexico, But More Than 130,000 Missing People Have Not
June 14, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Latin Times centers Madres Buscadoras at the World Cup, gives them the mic, lets the quotes land. Useful coverage of voices US outlets usually skip.

🇲🇽 The framing pins 130,000 missing on the current presidency without noting the crisis exploded in 2006 with Calderón's US-pressured drug war. The number predates Sheinbaum by 18 years.

• "Mexico, champion in disappearances"
• "the children of my fellow mothers, when will they return?"

AP/WAPO: Guadalajara Ramps Up Security and Promises Safe World Cup After Cartel Violence Scare
June 10, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Headline plays the cartel scare. The actual quotes are Mexican officials and residents reassuring visitors; AP avoids "narco-state" framing and notes 100,000+ security personnel deployed across host cities. The framing tax stays in the URL slug.

🇲🇽 February's violence followed the Mexican military killing the country's most powerful cartel boss — i.e., the state was effective. AP doesn't connect those dots.

• "It's important to remember that normalcy returned to the state in less than 48 hours" — Alfonso Briseño
• "We are going to be the safest" — Briseño

BLOOMBERG: Why Mexico's New Election Law Worries Democracy Advocates
June 14, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Bloomberg calls Mexico's anti-foreign-interference law a sign of Morena "consolidating power." Never mentioned: the US ambassador publicly commenting on Mexican domestic politics, DOJ indicting Morena officials, USAID money flowing to opposition NGOs. That's what the law actually responds to.

🔍 "Democracy advocates worry" is a recurring Bloomberg construction — an unnamed concerned class against a named elected government. The amendment passed the Chamber 307-128.

• "ruling Morena party's consolidation of power"
• elections "voided if the government believes foreign influence... affected the outcome"

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO AUTO PRODUCTION DOWN 3.7% IN MAY — BUT EXPORTS UP, DIVERSIFICATION KICKS IN</u>

INEGI: 342,926 light vehicles assembled in Mexico in May 2026, down 3.7% from a year earlier (13,187 fewer units). The headline reads bad — but exports went UP to 306,288 units (+1.7% annually), and YTD exports through May hit 1.39 million, up 4% on the year. The empire imposed auto tariffs to choke Mexico's industry; the industry diversified its buyers instead. Light trucks now make up 80% of national production. Five years ago that math would have been impossible.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>BAJA CALIFORNIA HITS #3 NATIONALLY FOR LOWEST INFORMAL EMPLOYMENT — INEGI</u>

INEGI confirmed Saturday that Baja California now ranks third in the country for lowest labor informality, with formal employment expanding under Governor Marina del Pilar Ávila Olmeda. Trump's tariffs were supposed to break Mexico's border industry — instead BC's export base, MSME support, and strategic location have kept it dynamic and competitive. Formal jobs with social security and benefits are the exact opposite of what Washington predicted nearshoring rollback would produce. The border economy isn't collapsing. It's consolidating.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE NUMBERS THE EMPIRE CAN'T STAND: 49% HOMICIDE DROP, 2.5% UNEMPLOYMENT, $23.5B FDI — WHY WASHINGTON WANTS THIS GOVERNMENT GONE</u>

Contralínea lays it out: under Sheinbaum's first year, FDI hit $23.591 billion, unemployment dropped to 2.5%, minimum wage is up 154% since 2018, homicides fell 49%, 29 new hospitals built, 42.8 million Mexicans covered by social welfare. Washington's response? CIA operations in Chihuahua without federal authorization, Standard & Poor's-led credit downgrades, "cognitive warfare" through US corporate media, and right-wing collaboration with foreign powers. Author Josafat Hernández: defending sovereignty against imperialism is the central task of the Mexican left. A government that delivers for its people is exactly the kind of government the empire targets.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM NAMES IT: ULTRADERECHA SECTORS ARE SABOTAGING THE MEXICO-US RELATIONSHIP</u>

President Sheinbaum directly accused far-right sectors on both sides of the border of running disinformation operations to wreck bilateral relations: "hay sectores de ultraderecha que son los que están buscando que no haya buena relación entre el gobierno de México y el de Estados Unidos." She named the LA Times and NYT — outlets running hit pieces since the AMLO years — and welcomed DHS denying a fabricated "special permit" claim targeting Sonora governor Durazo and Tamaulipas governor Villarreal. The PAN already filed an international complaint accusing AMLO of nonexistent narco ties. Same Brazil 2014 playbook, exposed in real time.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>KATIA ITZEL GARCÍA MAKES HISTORY: FIRST MEXICAN WOMAN TO ARBITRATE A MEN'S WORLD CUP</u>

The 33-year-old UNAM grad served as fourth official in Japan vs Netherlands at the Dallas stadium — becoming the first Mexican woman ever to arbitrate at a men's FIFA World Cup. One of 52 referees designated by FIFA for the 2026 tournament, García also officiated at the 2024 Paris Olympics, became the first woman to direct a men's Gold Cup match, and won Mexico's National Sports Award. From UNAM's Faculty of Political and Social Sciences to the world stage — public university producing world-class talent the empire can't manufacture.
